title: Toolchain boundaries
description: The bounded seams of the TypeScript/lint toolchain: who may import the legacy compiler API, which platforms must be proved natively, which tool-maintenance changes are admissible, and how an untrusted candidate is isolated while it is judged. It carries no package versions: the workspace catalog is the single version authority, and duplicating a pin here would create a second one.

compatibilityConsumers.description: The closed allowlist of repository files permitted to import the bounded TypeScript 6 compatibility API. Widening it is a reviewed change, never an implementation detail.

normalCompilerEntryPoints.description: Entry points that must resolve the NORMAL compiler. The compatibility package may never satisfy one of these.

platforms.description: Platforms whose command pack must execute NATIVELY. Cross-compilation, emulation, or metadata inspection is not proof.

onlyBuiltDependencies.description: Must remain empty. A package needing an install lifecycle script is a stop, not an exception to grant here.

maintenanceClasses.description: The CLOSED set of admissible tool-maintenance changes. A candidate may not union two classes to widen its admitted delta; the composite class exists precisely so a coupled change has one named, reviewed identity.

subjectIsolation.description: The contract for executing candidate tools as subjects under test. Two INDEPENDENT boundaries are required: a trust-domain boundary and an OS-level process boundary. A fresh runner alone satisfies neither.

processBoundary.description: Running the candidate as the launcher's own UID in the launcher's filesystem context is inadmissible and must be refused BEFORE execution.

protectedProjections.description: The universal protected floor: projections that EVERY maintenance class must preserve, whatever it otherwise allows. A path may appear here under one projection and in a class's allowedProjections under a different projection of the same file -- that is the point. Protecting `engine-mappings.json` wholesale would contradict the lint-engine class, which exists to let per-engine mapping detail move; protecting its policy/engine COVERAGE instead forbids the thing that actually matters, a policy quietly losing its mapping.

maintenanceVerifierAuthorities.description: AUTH-MAINTENANCE-VERIFIER. No maintenance class may admit a change to the authority that will judge it, so no class's allowedProjections may cover one of these paths. These paths are also the bootstrap condition: a predecessor that does not CONTAIN them cannot have produced the executable authority a maintenance claim is judged by, so classification against it is refused. That is a fact about where the executable authority came from, not a status bit inside the document -- a mutable flag would have to be flipped by some change, and no accepted task defines that transition.

subjectCommands.description: The exact commands the untrusted subject runs, owned by the PREDECESSOR. Candidate content never selects, adds to, or reorders this pack -- otherwise the thing under test would choose its own exam.

composite.description: True for a class that admits a coupled change which its parts could not admit separately.

allowedProjections.description: Exactly which projections of which paths MAY differ from the trusted predecessor. A changed path not covered here refuses the claim; prose in `allows` is a human summary and is never the check.

protectedProjections.description: Projections this class must preserve IN ADDITION to the universal floor.

lockRoots.description: The exact package roots whose deterministically derived transitive closure is the ONLY part of the resolved graph permitted to move.

composedOf.description: For a composite class only: the ids of the classes it couples. The composite must still preserve every protected projection of each contributing class -- coupling is not relaxation.

projection.description: A named function over repository content at one revision. Comparing the SAME projection across two revisions is what a maintenance claim is judged on.

bytes: the file's exact bytes. tree-bytes: the set of paths under a prefix and each one's bytes. mapping-coverage: the set of (policy, engine) pairs that carry a mapping, ignoring the vendor detail of each. mapping-detail: the per-engine vendor identity of each mapping row. catalog-pins: the pinned versions of the named packages. catalog-pins-except: every catalog pin OTHER than the named packages. lock-closure: lockfile entries reachable from the named roots.

packages.description: Package names selecting the projection, for the catalog and lock projections.

engines.description: Engine keys selecting the projection, for the mapping projections.
